extra.message: render_template_string is called with an f-string that interpolates request.path directly into the template source. Attackers can inject Jinja2 template expressions via the URL (e.g. '{{7*7}}') to achieve Server-Side Template Injection, leading to RCE.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: Flask secret_key is hardcoded to a static string 'super secret key'. This weakens session signing and allows session forgery if the source is disclosed.
Default user accounts are seeded with hardcoded weak passwords ('user' and 'admin'). The credentials are also visible in the source code repository.
A static registration code 'a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764' is hardcoded into the source, allowing anyone who can read the repository to register an account.
User-supplied search parameter from request.args is concatenated into a raw SQL fragment passed to sqlalchemy.text() in /search. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. ' OR 1=1 --).

The user-provided registration code is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to sqlalchemy.text(). An attacker can inject SQL via the 'registration_code' form field to bypass registration or extract data.

before_request deserializes a client-controlled 'preferences' cookie using pickle.loads. The cookie value is base64-decoded and then unpickled, allowing arbitrary code execution (RCE) on the server when an attacker crafts a malicious payload.

urlopen(url) fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL with no scheme/host validation. The /account/image endpoint forwards attacker-controlled URLs to this function, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary external hosts.

The /accounts/<int:user_id>/notes route returns all notes (including private ones) for any user_id supplied in the URL. There is no check that the authenticated user owns the requested user_id, allowing Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) disclosure of private notes belonging to other users.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /notes/<int:note_id>/delete endpoint deletes any note by ID without verifying that the requesting user owns the note or is an admin. Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary notes from any other user (IDOR / broken access control).

POST /account is missing @login_required, has no CSRF protection, and bulk-updates current_user.__dict__ with all form fields including 'is_admin'. A regular authenticated user can submit is_admin=on to elevate themselves to administrator (privilege escalation).

POST /darkmode is missing @login_required, allowing unauthenticated callers to invoke the handler. While the visible impact is limited, the route also touches g.preferences which is established in before_request and could be a stepping stone.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Note text is rendered with the | safe filter, bypassing Jinja2 auto-escaping. Because users create notes through the CKEditor (which produces HTML), any user can submit HTML/JavaScript that is stored and executed in every other user's browser (Stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: All state-changing POST endpoints (/account, /notes, /notes/<id>/delete, /registration-codes, /account/image, /signup, /login, /darkmode) use wtforms Form without CSRF protection, and CSRFProtect is not enabled. Although Flask-WTF is installed, none of the forms include CSRF tokens, enabling cross-site request forgery attacks.
SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, which logs every SQL statement (including parameters) to stdout. This can leak sensitive data such as credentials and PII to logs in production.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
